# `silk/time/zones_bundled`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The time zone database that the standard library carries: a `TimeZones` provider with the same
zones on every target.

## When to use

Provide [`BundledTimeZones`](#BundledTimeZones) when the result must not depend on the machine, or when the
machine may have no zone files, as in a slim container. `OsTimeZones` of
`silk.time.zones_native` already uses it on Windows, WASI, and browsers, where the system
has no zone files, and `PreferSystemTimeZones` uses it when the system does not know a zone.
Use `ZoneBundle` of `silk.time.zones_bundle` for a bundle that the program supplies.

## Details

The data is one release of the IANA time zone database, compiled to TZif files, with every
zone and link. The program holds it compressed, about 60 KB, and only a program that names
this provider holds it. The first lookup expands it one time, to about 230 KB, and the
provider keeps it. [`TimeZones.version`](./time-zones.md#TimeZones.version) names the release.

## Gotchas

- The release is the one of the Silk version that built the program. A zone rule that changed
  after that release is only in the files of the operating system.

## Examples

### Read a zone on any target

```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.time.instant { Instant }
import silk.time.zoned { ZonedDateTime }
import silk.time.zones { TimeZones, ZoneLookupError }
import silk.time.zones_bundled { BundledTimeZones }

// The hour in Rome at `at`.
effect fn romeHour(at: Instant) -> u8 ! ZoneLookupError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut TimeZones | &mut Allocator {
  let rome = run TimeZones.zone("Europe/Rome")
  return ZonedDateTime.make(at, &rome).time().hour()
}

effect fn failed(error: ZoneLookupError | OutOfMemoryError) -> u8 {
  return 255
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut zones = BundledTimeZones.make()
  let hour = run Effect.catchAll(romeHour(Instant.fromUnixSeconds(1795109782)), failed)
    |> Effect.provideMut<TimeZones>(&mut zones)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  if hour != 18 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `BundledTimeZones` with `import silk.time.zones_bundled { BundledTimeZones }`.

## `BundledTimeZones`

```silk
pub struct BundledTimeZones
```

The `TimeZones` provider with the time zone database inside the program.

### Details

[`BundledTimeZones.make`](#BundledTimeZones.impl.make) does no work. The first operation expands the data, and the
provider keeps it until it is dropped, so make one provider for the program and not one for
each lookup.

<a id="BundledTimeZones.impl.windowsZone"></a>

### Method `windowsZone`

```silk
pub effect fn windowsZone(self: &mut Self, name: &[u8]) -> Option<Bytes>
    ! ZoneLookupError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the IANA zone name for the zone name of Windows `name`, such as `Europe/Berlin`
for `W. Europe Standard Time`, or `None` if the table does not list the name. Letter case
does not matter.

#### Errors

- `ZoneLookupError` with the reason `InvalidData` if the data of the program is damaged.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the data or the name.
